We are an Islamic Science school for ages 3 to 11 that fosters curiosity and creativity in a nurturing Islamic environment.
About Oak Tree Primary School
Oak Tree Primary School is situated in a listed building, nestled within a leafy green pocket of South-West London, opposite Mitcham Cricket Green.
Our school differs from the traditional Islamic schools where Islamic studies and Quran are taught separately to the National Curriculum subjects.
Our vision is to develop a Muslim generation capable of analytical and critical thinking who will strive to fulfil their role positively and proudly in a multicultural Britain. We seek to achieve this by offering a curriculum where Islamic teachings are fully integrated with the National Curriculum, by constructing our lesson plans such that an Islamic value or teaching is a theme within our lessons, whether it be English, Geography, History, Science or PHSE. These Islamic values are then reinforced throughout school life, whether through school assemblies, themed days or weeks, or enrichment activities. Our children are empowered to discover themselves through Islam, achieve wholeness, spirituality and develop social consciousness, naturally choosing to be proud Muslims who give back to society.
We are proud to be a part of the Gardens of Jannah Trust federation of schools who also follow the same pioneering curriculum. The Gardens of Jannah Trust’s mission is to provide free education for the families and various services for the community.
Gardens of Jannah Trust School Magazine
We are delighted to present the inaugural edition of the Gardens of Jannah Trust School Magazine. This publication is a celebration of our community's journey and a showcase of the exceptional achievements and remarkable talents of our students for the academic year 2023/24.
In a this magazine, you will find a rich tapestry of stories that highlight our students' academic accomplishments, artistic endeavors, and extracurricular successes.
Discover how our educational initiatives and programs are shaping the future leaders of tomorrow. We are proud to share these moments and milestones with you.
Click HERE to access a PDF copy of the magazine. We hope you enjoy reading it as much as we enjoyed creating it.
Events and News
“As Muslims living in the UK we are part of the fabric of society. Islamic schools are of key importance to help develop a sense of belonging and a confident Muslim identity in our children. It is fantastic to see Oak Tree Primary School providing a nurturing environment that fosters both academic and religious excellence.”
Sheikh Dr Saalim Al-Azhari
"Oak Tree is another home away from home. My children have settled fast, are happy and love their teachers. My daughter was elected a Mental Health Ambassador which she is very excited about and I was pleased to hear from her there is a Calm Room for children to visit at lunch time."
"In the last two terms my children have visited the local library, BBC Earth, a local museum, the local park and the Science Museum, and I heard the older children went on an inspiring trip to Cambridge University. I am very pleased with the regularity and variety of educational trips. "
"As an Oak Tree mum I can say that I am very pleased with the new curriculum. My daughters are thriving with the way the school has established a positive classroom atmosphere. The lessons are well structured and we have noticed a huge change in our youngest who is in Reception, she is coming home with new knowledge everyday…especially about space the current topic! Both my daughters are very happy and with the help and support of the school are making great progress."
"When I first read through the Islamic studies curriculum documentation for Oak Tree and Gardens of Jannah Trust, I was blown away. I could see how it intended to integrate a comprehensive understanding of the Quran, Sunnah, and Islamic teachings. It showed a holistic approach to education, and nurturing not only intellectual development but also moral and ethical values. Traditional subjects like Science, History, Maths and English all having elements of Islamic concepts and values. Providing children with the foundations of the deen. Making Islam a way of life. "

pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher’s Welcome & Aims — Oak Tree Primary School
pageCache.text:
“Whoever takes a path in search of knowledge, Allah will facilitate for him a path to paradise.” (Muslim)
Headteacher’s Welcome and Aims
Welcome to Oak Tree Primary School – a pioneering and progressive Islamic faith based independent school. Our school is an exciting and stimulating place to be, offering a holistic education and high standards in academic achievement.
Through our tailored curriculum we aim to achieve the following:
God-conscious – Instil in our children awareness of Allah in all that they do; and understand that they are uniquely created by Allah and are loved and valued for who they are.
Knowledge - Develop knowledge and skills through an exciting, creative, integrated curriculum which fosters a lasting enjoyment of learning.
Islamic Values - Provide a distinctively Islamic environment within which children feel safe and happy and where faith, justice, respect, honesty, integrity, trust, compassion and love are valued and actively promoted within everyday learning.
Positive Relationships – Ingrain care, cooperation and respect for people and the environment, in particular developing a sensitivity to other peoples’ needs and points of view.
Confidence - Allow children to develop self-esteem by creating the conditions where children are emboldened to step out of their comfort zones always in a safe environment; where mistakes are opportunities for growth and resilience; and where success is aligned with perseverance and attitude rather than with outcome.
‘Can do’ attitude - Recognise, support and celebrate the achievements of our children equally whether they are creative, technologically skilled or academic as we recognise society has roles for all.
The outcome of the above aims, and what shapes our lesson plans and activities, is the endeavour to nurture and instil Islamic values into our children in the most natural way, showing them the true beauty of Islam, assisting in developing their inner beauty and character, alongside preparing our children for tomorrow’s challenges with exceptional academics.
Please do use the ‘Contact’ section to get in touch if you have any questions, and book a tour to meet us and see our school for yourself.

pageCache.pageTitle: Science Week 2025 — Oak Tree Primary School
pageCache.text:
Science Week 2025
Science Week 2025 was a thrilling experience for our students, filled with hands-on experiments, engaging workshops, and inspiring guest visits. Miss Hafsah captivated the children with an exciting experiment, combining hydrogen peroxide with a mixture of yeast and dish soap, creating a bubbling reaction that resembled lava flowing from a volcano.
Our younger students in Year 1 and 2 fully embraced the theme by dressing up as astronauts, doctors, nurses, and scientists, making their learning experience even more immersive.
Meanwhile, Year 5 and 6 took part in a Mad Science Workshop, where they explored static electricity and its fascinating effects. The highlight of the week was a special visit from Dr. Mohammed, who shared valuable insights into the wonders of science and its real-world applications.
The week was a fantastic opportunity for students to explore, investigate, and develop their curiosity about the world of science.

After School Clubs
We offer a variety of after school clubs. A sample list is shown below.
Clubs usually operate from 4.00 pm to 4.30 pm. The teacher who will be taking the club will collect the children at 3.45 pm (home time), the children will have a short break and are encouraged to bring a snack to eat prior to the start of club.
Payment and Commitment
As clubs are run by teachers or external coaches there are termly fees for each club. Fees must be paid termly in advance for a club, as clubs can only go ahead based on minimum numbers. Fees are non-refundable once the club has started.
Sample list of clubs:
STEM club - Inventors and Makers
In our self-led engineering club, pupils learn new STEM concepts through practical engineering and science activities, building future-proof skills like problem-solving and teamwork. We also teach children to love engineering and creativity, helping to inspire pupils towards successful futures in STEM Insha’Allah.
*Please contact the School Office for more information on current clubs and enrolment

pageCache.pageTitle: Islamic Curriculum & Hifdh Programme — Oak Tree Primary School
pageCache.text:
Islamic Curriculum & Hifdh Programme
“It will be said to the Companion of the Quran, when he enters Paradise: ‘Recite and rise one degree for every ayah,’ until he recites the last thing that he knows.” (Ibn Majah)
We believe the purpose of our Islamic curriculum is to mould a thinking, believing and practicing Muslim. Whilst we do have Islamic Studies as a subject and Arabic as a modern foreign language, these subjects do not sit separately, instead our unique lesson plans ensure Islamic values and teachings from Quran and hadith are embedded into lessons throughout the school day. Our whole school curriculum is designed with the aim that Eman and Taqwa are instilled in our students InshaAllah.
The school day begins for all primary children with Hifdh class which covers Quran reading and memorisation of the Quran.
Starting in Early Years, pupils are taught the 29 letters of the Arabic alphabet with the correct articulation (Makhakrij) and attributes (Siffat). We use the Qaeedah for Arabic reading and progress onto the correct and fluent reading of the Qur’an. The basic rules (Tajweed) of recitation are also taught and all pupils should leave the school being proficient in recitation of Quran and rules of Tajweed. Year 1 and 2 children are given extra lessons for Quran Reading each week in order to gain fluency.
In Early Years certain surahs and duas are memorised by all children and from Reception children have the option to join the hifdh programme. However the formal hifdh starts for all children from Year 1. The target is for children to have memorized Juz Amma by the age of 6-7, then moving onto the memorisation of the Ajza in descending order (i.e. Juzz 30, 29, 28, 27 and so on). The level of memorization is subject to a child’s personal ability as well as parental support. Parental support is entirely key to the progress each child will make in hifdh, for best results parents must ensure children are revising hifdh homework and practicing recitation at home daily.
The Islamic studies curriculum covers the following units of study: Aqeedah, Fiqh, Hadith, Seerah and Tafseer.
We provide a unique Tafseer programme that focuses on the understanding of the Surahs (Quranic chapters) that is implemented all the way from entry level in our Early Years up until the age of 11 when the child leaves primary education. In combination with the Hifdh programme our Islamic studies is designed such that the love of the Qur’an deepens and the children are able to appreciate its beauty. We want to focus our children on applying the Quran practically such that when they are presented with a question or faced with a dilemma the Quran is their first reference point. Our children will be equipped to navigate the Quran as an essential tool for problem solving in their daily lives. We pray that our children become living embodiments of the Qur’an.
Within our units we will also cover the 5 pillars of Islam, wudu, salat, stories and lessons from the lives of the Prophets, aspects of Islamic history and duas (supplications).
In addition to the above at Oak Tree we have devised a Nurture programme. The Islamic principles and units of study are carefully interwoven throughout the broad and balanced curriculum making it easy for the pupils to understand and enjoy the beauty of Islam. The holistic design enables pupils to become morally and socially aware of their role as a Muslim.
Please visit the following links from our Gardens of Jannah Trust website for further information on how we cultivate Islam into our childrens’ lives.
Information on our Tarbiyah curriculum please click the link below:
Seven Integrated Strands | GJT Education (gardensofjannahtrust.co.uk)
Information on our Key Principles:
Key Principles | GJT Education (gardensofjannahtrust.co.uk)
5D Islamic Programme
The 5D programme is a planning tool that is used to plan and teach a unique method that enables the child to derive certain character lessons from scientific knowledge.
It is based on the assumption that ideology-free science and authentic, Divinely revealed knowledge do not contradict each other, as they both come from the same source. It assumes that the universe is an eloquent book, replete with meaningful signs. It considers pure science to be an excellent way of revealing the Divine signs which make up the book of the universe. Children will gain a new understanding of scientific knowledge through 5D thinking which comprises: 1) analytical thinking; 2) analogical thinking; 3) critical thinking; 4) meditative thinking; and 5) moral thinking. The 5D thinking approach is expected to function like 5D glasses, showing multiple dimensions of reality and wellbeing through our foundation and science lessons.
At Oak Tree we have daily morning worship which starts after the hifdh lesson. The class begins with the recitation of the names of Allah and recitation of the Quran. On Jumuah, Morning Worship also consists of the recitation of Surah ‘Kahf ‘ and ‘Durood ‘ (salutations upon Prophet Muhammad peace be upon him). Year 5 and 6 children are encouraged to memorise Surah Kahf on Jumuah.
Assemblies play an important part in the life of the school with the whole school coming together. They serve to emphasise and reinforce collectively the school’s strong Islamic ethos and social & moral values. Assemblies are a wonderful opportunity to get the children involved and develop public speaking skills, each week members of a different class will present on the Assembly topic.
The children are already taught the Arabic alphabet as part of the hifdh programme. They progress to learn the Arabic numbers as well as basic vocabulary, initiating the use of nouns in their daily conversation, followed by verbs and heading towards making useful sentences. We use a variety of resources available to us both from UK and Egypt.
From year one onwards our children pray salah in congregation each day. We hope to inculcate this spiritually purifying and self-reflective habit for life by adhering to this compulsory pillar of Islam and revolving the school day around it.

pageCache.pageTitle: Whole School Curriculum — Oak Tree Primary School
pageCache.text:
Whole School Curriculum
Our curriculum aims to prepare our children as world citizens of the 21st Century.
As an Islamic school, the principles of Islamic education remain at our core. This includes the pursuit of excellence. To achieve this, our children need high levels of literacy and numeracy. Our broad and balanced curriculum is designed to unlock the potential of every child. There is flexibility in curriculum planning so that teachers can address identified gaps in knowledge and skills. Specific recovery and feedback sessions are scheduled into weekly class timetables to give teachers the space to give individualised attention and act swiftly to address any potential gap and provide challenge activities for greater depth pupils. We have high academic expectations for all our pupils, with the majority, at the very least, mastering age-related expectations.
Our bespoke curriculum developed over many years is based on and complies with all requirements of the National Curriculum and EYFS Framework, and is supplemented to bring in Islamic teachings or viewpoints into the majority of our lessons. It is a highly ambitious and inspiring framework for our exceptional teachers to act within; with positive teacher/pupil relationships and communication at the core. Our curriculum covers Literacy (English), Numeracy (Maths), Science, History, Geography, Computer Science, Art, PSHE, RE and Physical Education.
Unique Lesson Planning
We have introduced a unique 5-dimensional approach to our teaching methodologies which is designed to incorporate independent and critical thinking, and Islamic values. This methodology is being used across our foundation subjects. The approach consists of leading the pupils through a 5-stage process for any given topic: 1. Explore (analyse) 2. Compare (consider analogies) 3. Question (critical thinking) 4. Connect (link to Quran / Islamic teachings) 5. Appreciate (morals and values). Please see an example of a 5-d lesson plan for more information. [Hyperlink to camel lesson]
Our Thematic approach
We want our children to make links and transfer their skills and knowledge from one subject to another. Therefore, at our school much learning takes place in cross-curricular lessons based on a theme. Each term every class studies a different theme; some are science based, some are historical, and others have a geographical bias. Over the course of a year, pupils will experience one of each, having the opportunity to gain a depth of knowledge on a particular topic and therefore encouraging deeper debate and thinking. The themes are exciting and pupils have the opportunity to help to plan them from time to time.
In addition to the class themes, our curriculum includes themed weeks and days which are a focus for the whole school. These special themes reflect the context of the school and our local community, some examples include: Eid, Black history week, Charity week, Maths week, International week, Science Week, Multi-media week, Be Healthy Week, Islam awareness week, Book week and so forth. Again these themed weeks/days are used to reinforce Islamic and British values that the children have been learning about.
What are we learning?
We have a curriculum overview for every half term, have a look at what we are teaching below. [Insert table for Cycle A and Cycle B from https://www.evergreenprimary.org.uk/what-we-are-learning/]
Flip Learning
At Oak Tree we employ flip learning across our subjects, a cutting-edge approach in teaching methodologies. Flipped learning is an approach in which the conventional notion of classroom-based learning is inverted so that students are introduced to the learning material before class with classroom time then being used to deepen understanding through discussion with peers and problem-solving activities facilitated by teachers. As a result parents are also more engaged and have a better knowledge of what their children are being taught. Please see Flip Learning and Homework [https://www.evergreenprimary.org.uk/flip-learning-portal/] for examples of the flip learning which is provided for each Year group in advance of the class taking place. The topic is then consolidated in school with the teacher and then consolidated once again with Homework which is set once a week and available on the above link.
Assessment and Monitoring
Assessment is a continuous part of the school year and records are kept for each subject and child. Teachers and pupils use target mapping to track knowledge and skills and record pupil outcomes. This is used precisely by teachers to inform and plan the next steps in each pupil’s learning so as to ensure pupils meet and exceed the expected end point. As the sizes of the classes are small, the teachers are able to closely monitor the progress of each child (academic as well as social/emotional) and support them appropriately. The progress pupils are making in Reading, Writing and Mathematics along with their personal development is reviewed half termly in Achievement Team meetings with SLT, where the progress of every child is discussed, but especially individual vulnerable pupils, and interventions agreed to bridge attainment and progress gaps.
This continuous monitoring and scrutiny by the teacher, Subject Leaders and SLT ensures that high expectation and demanding outcomes are maintained. In-school and cross-school moderation is also quality assured across the Gardens of Jannah Trust federation of schools by Subject Leaders and external consultants, this includes working groups for Mathematics, English and EYFS.
Formal parent-teacher meetings and progress reports are given twice a year.
Excellent Pastoral Care
Pastoral care, the emotional and physical wellbeing of our pupils, is at the heart of our curriculum. Pupils’ spiritual, moral, social and cultural development is a priority for our teachers. Our pupils show themselves to be deep thinkers. Particularly in RE and PSHE, they show a keen interest in ethical issues and can apply their personal values to situations, giving reasons for their decisions and actions. They are ready to question arguments and situations, and are encouraged to see points of views and beliefs other than their own. In recognising the holistic development of the whole-child, the pastoral support given to children so they can access the curriculum is exceptionally strong, with particular attention to vulnerable children. The school has various systems which support the emotional and mental well-being of children and provides signposting to their parents.

pageCache.pageTitle: Early Years — Oak Tree Primary School
pageCache.text:
Join a loving, caring, safe and happy environment where your child will truly thrive.
At Oak Tree, we pride ourselves on our interactive and stimulating Early Years (Nursery and Reception) curriculum which allows for many ‘I wonder’ moments.
Our curriculum shaped over many years, is all about building the foundations for an Islamic personality whilst fostering well-being, self-confidence, communication and academic success.
Our class sizes are small, providing a huge amount of individualised attention
All staff within EY hold an early year’s qualification
Our Early Years facility contained all across one level of the School allows the children to safely and fluidly move around our play, sensory, learning and art zones
Our dedicated Early Years Outdoor Play Area contains areas for learning; a mud kitchen; planting; eating; and of course play!
We are a through-school enabling Nursery and Reception children to stay with us all through Primary.
As childrens’ education experts for over 20 years, our knowledge and tailored approach to developing children through exploration; communication and thinking is woven into everything that we do, starting in Early Years, laying the foundations for them to become thoughtful, global citizens in a modern Britain.
Learning
The children within our Early Years are given the autonomy to make choices and learn through a range of play based opportunities. We also encourage play in mixed age groups, which provide a traditional large family atmosphere, helping children to acquire social and emotional skills.
Daily
In Nursery there are two carpet sessions (morning and afternoon), which cover phonics, communication and mathematics. Most of our children will be on the reading journey prior to reaching Reception.
In Reception, there are four daily whole class teaching carpet sessions that include handwriting, phonics, mathematics and literacy.
Phonics is taught through the Little Wandle Letters and Sounds programme of study and Mathematics is based on White Rose maths.
Weekly
We have poetry sessions, nasheeds, building blocks of Islamic belief; Surahs and stories from Quran, Arabic letters, Arabic as a language and PE.
We follow the EYFS framework and our Islamic ethos permeates each child’s day.

pageCache.pageTitle: House System — Oak Tree Primary School
pageCache.text:
House System
Every child is placed in a House as soon as he or she starts their journey at Oak Tree. Houses are essential in creating community spirit and give the children an opportunity to contribute to something bigger that involves children from all year groups. We reinforce our school value of giving back by supporting the children to raise money for the three House charities chosen annually. The House system also entails some friendly rivalry as the children compete to gain points for behaviour, effort and good deeds.
Our Houses are Salahudeen Ayubi, Dhul Karnain and Umar Farook. Each House is represented by their House Captains (voted in annually) and supported by a member of staff who acts as House Leader.
Every week, the House points are counted by our House Captains and a weekly winner announced during Assembly. House points are then tallied over the course of a term, a winner is announced, and the children in that House are rewarded. At the end of the year, once all House points are tallied, the House Champions are announced.
The Gardens of Jannah Trust federation of schools all operate the same House System so that there are more opportunities for the children to interact and cooperate when inter-school events are held.

pageCache.pageTitle: Charity week — Oak Tree Primary School

About Oak Tree Primary School
Oak Tree Primary School is situated in a listed building, nestled within a leafy green pocket of South-West London, opposite Mitcham Cricket Green.
Our school differs from the traditional Islamic schools where Islamic studies and Quran are taught separately to the National Curriculum subjects.
Our vision is to develop a Muslim generation capable of analytical and critical thinking who will strive to fulfil their role positively and proudly in a multicultural Britain. We seek to achieve this by offering a curriculum where Islamic teachings are fully integrated with the National Curriculum, by constructing our lesson plans such that an Islamic value or teaching is a theme within our lessons, whether it be English, Geography, History, Science or PHSE. These Islamic values are then reinforced throughout school life, whether through school assemblies, themed days or weeks, or enrichment activities. Our children are empowered to discover themselves through Islam, achieve wholeness, spirituality and develop social consciousness, naturally choosing to be proud Muslims who give back to society.
We are proud to be a part of the Gardens of Jannah Trust federation of schools who also follow the same pioneering curriculum. The Gardens of Jannah Trust’s mission is to provide free education for the families and various services for the community.
Gardens of Jannah Trust School Magazine
We are delighted to present the inaugural edition of the Gardens of Jannah Trust School Magazine. This publication is a celebration of our community's journey and a showcase of the exceptional achievements and remarkable talents of our students for the academic year 2023/24.
In a this magazine, you will find a rich tapestry of stories that highlight our students' academic accomplishments, artistic endeavors, and extracurricular successes.
Discover how our educational initiatives and programs are shaping the future leaders of tomorrow. We are proud to share these moments and milestones with you.
Click HERE to access a PDF copy of the magazine. We hope you enjoy reading it as much as we enjoyed creating it.
Events and News
“As Muslims living in the UK we are part of the fabric of society. Islamic schools are of key importance to help develop a sense of belonging and a confident Muslim identity in our children. It is fantastic to see Oak Tree Primary School providing a nurturing environment that fosters both academic and religious excellence.”
Sheikh Dr Saalim Al-Azhari
"Oak Tree is another home away from home. My children have settled fast, are happy and love their teachers. My daughter was elected a Mental Health Ambassador which she is very excited about and I was pleased to hear from her there is a Calm Room for children to visit at lunch time."
"In the last two terms my children have visited the local library, BBC Earth, a local museum, the local park and the Science Museum, and I heard the older children went on an inspiring trip to Cambridge University. I am very pleased with the regularity and variety of educational trips. "
"As an Oak Tree mum I can say that I am very pleased with the new curriculum. My daughters are thriving with the way the school has established a positive classroom atmosphere. The lessons are well structured and we have noticed a huge change in our youngest who is in Reception, she is coming home with new knowledge everyday…especially about space the current topic! Both my daughters are very happy and with the help and support of the school are making great progress."
"When I first read through the Islamic studies curriculum documentation for Oak Tree and Gardens of Jannah Trust, I was blown away. I could see how it intended to integrate a comprehensive understanding of the Quran, Sunnah, and Islamic teachings. It showed a holistic approach to education, and nurturing not only intellectual development but also moral and ethical values. Traditional subjects like Science, History, Maths and English all having elements of Islamic concepts and values. Providing children with the foundations of the deen. Making Islam a way of life. "

Admissions
Join our family!
At Gardens of Jannah Trust, we aim to create schools all over the world that serve as pillars of support for the Muslim community, providing every child with access to high-quality education and comprehensive welfare programmes. Our mission is to empower the next generation through free education, fostering a sense of belonging, resilience, and community spirit.
Admission Arrangements
We know that choosing a school is a big decision for any parent and that the process of school admissions can be confusing. We are here to help you as much as we can and make the process as seamless as possible. If you have any queries, or would like to book a tour please do not hesitate to contact the School Office on admin@oaktreeprimarysch.co.uk or call on: 020 8648 4647 or 07429 112 217.
Policy Overview: Oak Tree entrance
Gardens of Jannah Trust is dedicated to offering education to children in the Muslim community. We believe that education is a fundamental right and strive to eliminate any financial barriers that may prevent children from receiving quality educational opportunities.
We have been successful in providing free educational services for almost 12 years, positively impacting the lives of numerous children and their families within our community.
2 Welfare Programmes:
In addition to academic education, we provide a variety of welfare programmes designed to support the holistic development of our students. These programmes include mentorship, counselling, and extracurricular activities that cater to the diverse needs of our community.
3 School Placement Policy:
Admission to our schools is granted on a first-come, first-served basis.
We prioritise our services for families who are on a low income or those facing asylum and those from underserved backgrounds to ensure they receive the necessary support to thrive. By offering tailored services and wraparound support, we empower these children to overcome challenges and achieve their full potential, both academically and personally.
4 Wraparound Care Priority for Working Parents:
We recognise the challenges working parents face in balancing their professional responsibilities with their children's educational needs. To support these families, we prioritise wraparound care services that extend beyond regular school hours. This includes after-school clubs, homework assistance, and holiday programmes, allowing parents to work with peace of mind knowing their children are in a safe and nurturing environment. We aim to provide flexible solutions to meet the needs of working parents while ensuring that their children receive quality care and support.
5 Community Engagement:
We actively encourage community involvement and collaboration. Parents, guardians, and community members are invited to participate in school events, volunteer programmes, and decision-making processes to foster a strong sense of community ownership and support.
To run our services and sustain our programmes, we welcome donations and rely on support from local businesses and the community. Your contributions play a vital role in helping us achieve our vision and fulfil our mission. To donate, please contact us at info@gardensofjannahtrust.co.uk or reach out to our office at 02037597408. We invite you to support us in our efforts to provide quality education and welfare programmes for our students and their families.
7 Continuous Improvement:
Gardens of Jannah Trust is committed to continuously evaluating and improving our services to meet the evolving needs of our students and the community. We welcome feedback and suggestions to enhance our educational and welfare programmes.
Commitment to Inclusivity:
At Gardens of Jannah Trust, we recognise the importance of inclusivity and diversity. We are dedicated to creating an environment where every individual feels welcomed, valued, and supported, regardless of their background. Our programmes are designed to be accessible and responsive to the unique needs of all community members.
By adhering to this policy, Gardens of Jannah Trust aims to create a nurturing and empowering environment that supports the growth and development of every child in our community, ensuring they have the resources and opportunities to thrive. We believe that through collaboration, support, and a shared commitment to education, we can make a meaningful difference in the lives of our students and their families.
Together, we can build a brighter future for our community and foster a generation that is well-equipped to face the challenges of tomorrow. Thank you for your support and commitment to our mission.

FAQ
What are the school timings for pupils?
All primary children and EY Hifdh children - 7.45 am
EY (Nursery & Reception) children - 8.25 am
School pick-up times:
Year 1 and Year 2 – 3.30pm
Year 3 and Year 4 – 3.40 pm
Year 5 and Year 6 – 3.45 pm
How do I report my child as absent?
Please inform the School Office on the number or email above before 7.45 am if your child is going to be absent with the reason for absence.
What happens if my child is late?
If your child is going to be late to school please inform the School Office on the number or email above before 7.45 am. If the school gate has closed by the time your child arrives then their parent/guardian will have to wait with them until 8.30 am to be allowed into school. This is so that disruption to Hifdh class is minimised.
If you are late to pick up your child at the end of the day, please also inform School Office so we can let your child and the teacher know
What food can I send for my child to eat at break/lunch?
Please note we are a nut free school. We promote healthy eating in our school so sugary snacks/drinks, chocolates, crisps are not allowed except on Jumuah. Fridays is Jumuah so a treat day, where one treat e.g. packet of crisps is allowed, but please do not send family size packets of sweets, crisps etc.
Please do send a water bottle each day and label with your child’s name.
When does my child have to do homework?
Homework is required to be submitted once per week, your child’s teacher will let them know which day their homework should be sent in. The homework and flip learning is available on our website. In addition all primary children have a spelling test once per week, the class teacher will inform them which day of the week.
When are school fees due?
School fees are due in advance or if paying in monthly instalments then at the latest by the 10th of each month.
Is there a notice period if my child has to leave the school?
One full term’s notice is required for the withdrawal of a child from school. This notice should be received by the School in writing on or before the first day of term. If such notice is not given, a term’s fees in lieu of notice will become due. We also reserve the right to withhold any deposit if this is not upheld.
